messages:
pagerbot: PAGER — INC-1943218888 — Unusual auth failure spike detected. 401/403 rate > 8x baseline from 3 distinct external IPs hitting /v1/stream and /v1/chat. oncall=sara, severity=high

sara: oncall here, I see the page. Ack. Spinning up triage. @mike can you pull prod ingress logs + recent deploys?

mike: pulling logs now. quick note — ingress shows repeated malformed auth headers + rapid token reuse. IPs: 198.51.100.12, 203.0.113.45, 198.51.100.99.

daniel: Security here. Initial hypothesis: either leaked service tokens or a log-forwarder exposed header fragments to an external indexer. Eva, can you check the logshipper indexer outputs?

eva: checking logshipper. Found an indexer export job to s3://telemetry-collection-arch with an ACL change at 01:14UTC. A subset of requests (headers) were included in the export. Looks like a staging forwarder job accidentally pointed at prod bucket.

tina: Support chiming in — no customer facing 5xxs reported yet, but a handful of customers reported auth failures starting ~01:12UTC. Might be correlated.

ryan: running quick search for token reuse — matched 42 sessions where same bearer token used across multiple IPs. Looks suspicious.

sara: okay immediate actions: 1) block the three source IPs at WAF, 2) disable the export job, 3) rotate the staging->prod forwarder credentials, 4) rotate service tokens that appear in exported logs. Assigning tasks: @mike take WAF + block, @eva disable export and snapshot bucket, @daniel coordinate token rotation plan.

mike: WAF rules pushed for those IPs, temporary rule to block the endpoints. Confirmed blocks at 01:28UTC. Added logging rule to capture future hits.

eva: export job disabled and job schedule paused at 01:30UTC. Snapshot of the bucket taken and put into internal-forensics s3://sec-quarantine/INC-1943218888. Preserved object list and ACL history.

daniel: preparing immediate key rotation for the forwarder service account and any service tokens seen in export. List coming in <5m. Julie (legal) — do you want to be looped for potential PII exposure?

julie: Legal here — yes please loop. Need a preliminary list of affected customers + what fields were exported. Add me to the incident bridge.

sara: @mike can you create short-lived policy to force refresh for tokens issued between 00:45-01:30UTC for the forwarder service and dependent services? 

mike: creating token revoke job now. Will push invalidation for tokens with last use in that window. ETA 8m.

ops-bot: Deploybot: rolled back telemetry-forwarder image from sha:abc123 -> sha:abc100 at 01:35UTC per request. No other infra deploys in that window.

ryan: pulled the export artifacts — redacted headers show truncated bearer tokens, IPs, paths. No full request bodies observed. Still potential user-identifiers in headers (x-customer-id).

daniel: map of exposure: headers + x-customer-id for ~2,600 requests over 45 minutes. Need to treat as possible sensitive leakage. Plan: rotate impacted API keys, notify customers scoped to those x-customer-ids, prepare CS template.

tina: drafting customer-facing note — short, transparent, no technical details beyond impacted time window. Will coordinate with legal and comms.

sara: any sign of active exploitation beyond brute reuse? mike/ryan?

mike: we see token bouncing across many geo-locations quickly, suggests token scraping then reuse. Blocks have reduced hit rate to baseline. No new spikes last 10m.

eva: forensics captured file checksums and object ACL change logs. We'll hand over access to sec for deeper analysis.

daniel: next: rotate keys, run scans for other misconfigured forwarder jobs, patch the deployment automation to prevent cross-environment bucket targets. Also propose adding a pre-deploy ACL check.

julie: legal requests customer list and full artifact manifest. Also advise preserving chain-of-custody for evidence; do not delete original objects in quarantine.

sara: ops summary for timeline to share: 00:45UTC — first anomalous auth; 01:12UTC — export job ran; 01:14UTC — ACL change on s3 bucket; 01:28UTC — WAF blocks applied; 01:30UTC — export job disabled; 01:35UTC — forwarder rollback + token invalidate started.

ryan: adding recommended mitigations to runbook: enforce least-privilege for forwarder, require explicit target env in deploy configs, automated ACL linting, and sampling scrubber to strip sensitive headers before export.

tina: Customer impact: flagging subset of customers for targeted outreach (approx 120 x-customer-ids). No PII confirmed yet but potential. Comms will run through legal.

daniel: I've kicked off token rotation for affected keys and created a short-lived allowlist to monitor replays. Also starting an internal audit for other exporters.

sara: creating a follow-up incident call in 30m to review investigation. For now severity remains high P1 until we finish customer outreach and confirm no ongoing exploitation. Thanks all — please post any new artifacts into the quarantine S3 path and update the incident doc. :thumbsup:

mike: noted. Posting logs to s3://sec-quarantine/INC-1943218888/logs/ and will update incident doc.

eva: forensic copy uploaded, will not alter original.

julie: legal on bridge in 5. Preparing shortlist of regulatory triggers if customer data confirmed.

sara: closing handoff from initial pager -> oncall triage. Next actions: customer notifications (tina + legal), full token rotate (daniel + mike), root cause remediation (eva + eng infra), postmortem plan (sara).

pagerbot: Incident update: page acknowledged and mitigations applied. Monitoring for 60m.

sara: thanks team — I'll keep the thread updated and spin up the postmortem doc after bridge.
